items.headline: Israel's president asks Eisenkot, not Netanyahu, to form a government
items.summary: Isaac Herzog chose former army chief Gadi Eisenkot after 67 MPs backed him against 46 for Netanyahu. He has 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension, to build a 61-seat coalition.

items.headline: US sets up task force to cut Iran's overland supply routes
items.summary: US Central Command launched Task Force Iron Gate to stop weapons and sanctioned goods reaching Iran by land and across the Caspian Sea. It extends the US naval blockade of Iranian ports.

items.headline: Cost-of-living protests draw over 140,000 across France
items.summary: The interior ministry counted about 146,000 marchers on Saturday, 46,000 of them in Paris; unions said 250,000. The protests over fuel prices and living standards began with school students in September.

items.headline: Poundland's future hangs on rescue talks
items.summary: The chain of about 600 shops and 11,000 staff has filed notice to appoint administrators while its US owner Gordon Brothers weighs bids. Tesco, B&M and Poundstretcher are among those interested in parts of the business.

items.headline: Berkshire Hathaway profit falls as share buybacks double
items.summary: Operating profit fell 6% to $12.71bn in the third quarter, while the company bought back $9.6bn of its own shares. It bought about $2bn more in October.

items.headline: Jet fuel costs cut profits at British Airways owner IAG
items.summary: Pre-tax profit fell 12.9% to €1.63bn in the three months to September as fuel costs rose 30.4%, outpacing a 4.5% rise in revenue. The boss still called the outlook positive.

items.headline: AI-assisted proofs challenge a key computer science assumption
items.summary: OpenAI and Anthropic papers claim to disprove the 1998 Exponential Time Hypothesis, with heavy AI involvement. The proofs passed machine checks and are now under review by experts, including the hypothesis's co-author.
items.source: AI Weekly (citing the New York Times), 7 Nov

items.headline: Elvis estate and Eminem's publisher sue AI music firm Suno
items.summary: Two US lawsuits accuse Suno of letting users clone Presley's voice and of copying about 269 Eminem songs. Suno says it exists to help people make original music.

items.headline: Report questions Chinese firms cleared to buy Nvidia AI chips
items.summary: A New York Times investigation found some of the roughly two dozen Chinese firms licensed for Nvidia H200 chips had empty offices or links to blacklisted groups. US officials say every application is carefully reviewed.
items.source: AI Weekly (citing the New York Times), 7 Nov
